full_judgment:
7. It appears that it was argued by the appellant in the High Court Division that the application before the Rin Salishi Board was not barred by time as wrongly held by the Courts below because the Board started functioning after 3(three) months of its constitution and, as such, the limitation of 6 (six) months as provided under section 7 of the Act should be counted from the date of functioning of the Board and not from the date of its constitution. The High Court Division did not agree with the contention and upheld the findings of the Courts below that the application under section 7 of the Act was barred by time and that the Rin Salishi Board had acted without jurisdiction in entertaining the application as rightly held by the lower appellate Court. 

 8. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate for the appellant, obtained leave to appeal, urging two grounds; one is that the Courts below as also the High Court Division erred in holding that the application before the Board was time barred and the second ground is that even if the application was barred by limitation the Rin Salishi Board having jurisdiction over the subject-matter and the parties the decision of the Board is not without jurisdiction and that the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to interfere with the decision of a quasi-judicial tribunal in view of the finality attached to the said decision by section 19(1) of Act. 

 9. Mr. Islam while arguing the appeal, however, decided not to press the second ground and to confine his submission to the first ground only. Mr. Islam developed his submission on the question of limitation with reference to the Act and the Rules made thereunder. He referred to section 7(1) of the Act which, inter alia, provides that an application under this section has to be filed before the Board within six months of its constitution in accordance with the procedure prescribed by the Rules. The relevant Rules are Rules 3, 9(1), 11(3) and 12 of the Bangladesh Rin Salishi Bidhimala, 1989. Rule 3 provides that an application for the purposes mentioned therein has to be filed before the Board constituted in the Upazila of the applicant within 6 (six) months of the constitution of the said Board. Rule 9 (1) provides that the applicant has to file the application to the Chairman of the Board either personally or through his authorized agent at the time and place of the sitting of the Board. Rule 11(3) provides that upon constitution of the Board by the Government by notification, the concerned collector would notify by order the place, date and time of the first sitting of the Board and would send copies of the Government Notification and his order to the Chairman and members of the Board and further would arrange wide publicity in the locality of the substance of his order. Mr. Islam finally referred to Rule 12 which requires the Chairman of the Board to examine the applicant upon receiving his application and to enter the substance of the relief claimed in the prescribed form if satisfied with the merit of the application and to cause service of notice upon the other side and if not satisfied with the merit of the application, to reject the same forthwith. 

 10. It is not disputed that the Rin Salishi Boards including that for Bauphal PS were constituted by a Gazette Notification dated 27 May, 1989. It has been noticed that under section 7(1) of the Act an application thereunder has to be filed, inter alia, within 6(six) months of the constitution of Board. Admittedly the appellant filed his application before the Board on 18-5-90 clearly beyond 6(six) months of the constitution of the Board. Mr Islam has submitted that for the purpose of limitation, along with the requirement of 6(six) months time from the date of the constitution of the Board the other requirement under the same section 7 of the Act that the application has to be filed in accordance with the procedure prescribed by the Rules has also to be satisfied. The provisions of the relevant Rules as mentioned above clearly indicate that an application cannot be presented to the Board unless the sitting of the Board actually takes place after the collector concerned notifies about the place, date and time of the sitting of the Board. The applicant has to be examined by the Chairman of the Board immediately on receipt of the application and if the application is found unsatisfactory the same is liable to be dismissed forthwith. 

 11. In the instant case, it is found from the certificate given by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Bauphal dated 12 December, 1996 that the Rin Salishi Board, Bauphal Upazila was inaugurated by the Deputy Commissioner, Patuakhali on 4-1-90 from which date the Board started functioning. Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, learned Advocate-on-Record for the respondents, has not disputed the contents of the said certificate. Therefore, if the limitation is counted, and the submission of Mr. Islam is persuasive enough to so count, from the said date ie, 4-1-90 and not from the date of the constitution of the Board on 27-5-89, it cannot be said that the application of the defendant-appellant before the Board was time-barred. Mr. Chaklader has found it difficult to resist the force of the submission of Mr. Islam that the Courts below as well as the High Court Division have wrongly construed the period of limitation by merely looking partly to the provisions of section 7 of the Act and overlooking the other provisions read with the rules and thus allowed themselves to fall into an error. Mr. Chaklader finding no other way argued, as if for argument''s sake, that even if the application before the Board was not time-barred, it was not maintainable because the defendant was not a এ কৃষক as required under section 7 of the Act. This point can hardly be raised at this stage because it seems that neither any objection has been taken on that account nor any finding has been recorded by any Court in that behalf. It has been noticed that the decision in the suit mainly turned on the question whether the application filed by the defendant before the Board was barred by limitation. Now it has been found by us that the limitation was wrongly construed by all the Courts and that the application of the defendant under section 7 of the Act was not time-barred. The suit of the plaintiff must accordingly fail.
